about: OutSystems is a low-code application development platform that lets enterprises build, deploy and manage web and mobile applications quickly, with AI-assisted development tools. It sells subscriptions to large organisations in financial services, insurance, healthcare, government and retail, with several thousand customers worldwide. Founded in Portugal in 2001 and now headquartered in Boston, it is backed by KKR and Tiger Global (valued at around 9.5 billion dollars in 2021) and has well over 1,000 employees. B2B software with little consumer awareness.

Arqiva is a UK communications infrastructure and media services company. It owns and operates the national terrestrial TV and radio broadcast transmission network, thousands of towers and masts, and is a major provider of smart metering communications and satellite and media services. Customers include broadcasters, mobile operators and utilities. It is headquartered near Winchester, Hampshire, and has been owned by a consortium including Macquarie, IFM and Ontario Teachers' pension plan. B2B infrastructure brand with moderate recognition in the UK media sector.

Collibra is a data intelligence and governance software company, offering a platform for data catalogues, data quality and privacy compliance used by large enterprises in finance, pharma and government. Founded in 2008 in Brussels, it is now headquartered in New York, with a valuation of 5.25 billion dollars after its 2021 funding round led by ICONIQ, Index Ventures and Tiger Global. B2B software with no consumer visibility.

Gong is a revenue intelligence software company that records and analyses sales calls, meetings and emails with AI to give sales teams insight on deals and coaching. Founded in 2015 in Israel by Amit Bendov and Eilon Reshef, it is headquartered in San Francisco and valued at 7.25 billion dollars in 2021. Customers are B2B sales organisations, with thousands of enterprise accounts. Investors include Coatue, Sequoia, Salesforce Ventures and Thrive. B2B software brand with strong awareness in sales technology but none among consumers.

Highspot is a sales enablement platform that helps sellers find content, prepare for meetings and coach reps, with AI features, serving enterprise sales organisations. Founded in 2012 in Seattle, Washington, it has raised more than 640 million dollars, with backers including Salesforce Ventures, Tiger Global, Shasta and Bain Capital Ventures. In 2024-2025 it moved into acquisitions, including merging with Seismic-like competitors. B2B software with some visibility in sales technology circles, no consumer awareness.

about: Skillsoft is a corporate learning and talent development company providing online courses, books, videos, coaching and AI-powered skill assessments to businesses and governments. It owns Global Knowledge training and Codecademy, and was combined with Churchill Capital Corp II in a 2021 SPAC deal; listed on the NYSE (SKIL). Based in Nashua, New Hampshire, with tens of thousands of enterprise customers and around 2,000 employees. B2B learning provider, widely known among HR and L&D teams, little consumer visibility outside Codecademy.

6sense is a B2B revenue marketing and sales intelligence platform that uses AI and intent data to identify accounts that are in the market to buy and to orchestrate account-based marketing. Founded in 2013 and headquartered in San Francisco, it counts several thousand enterprise customers, and was valued at 5.2 billion dollars in 2021, backed by Sapphire Ventures, Insight Partners, Tiger Global and others. B2B software brand, well known among marketers, no consumer awareness.

Cyxtera Technologies was a data centre and colocation operator, spun out of CenturyLink's assets in 2017 and owned by BC Partners, with about 60 facilities worldwide and the Cyxtera Cyber fabric. It listed through a SPAC with Starboard Value Acquisition Corp. in 2021 (Nasdaq: CYXT). It filed for Chapter 11 in June 2023, and its assets were largely acquired by Brookfield Infrastructure in 2023. Based in Coppell, Texas, previously Coral Gables, Florida. B2B infrastructure with limited public awareness.

Degreed is a learning experience platform that lets employees aggregate and track learning from many sources, with skills tracking and career development tools for enterprises. Founded in 2012 and based in Pleasanton, California, it has raised around 460 million dollars from investors such as Sapphire Ventures, Insight and Owl Ventures. Customers include large corporate clients, with millions of learners. B2B software that is little known to consumers.

Edgio was a content delivery network and edge cloud company formed in 2022 when Limelight Networks acquired Edgecast (from Apollo) and rebranded. It served video streaming, web security and application acceleration to media and software customers. Based in Phoenix, Arizona, it listed on Nasdaq (EGIO) but struggled with debt and weak revenue, filed for Chapter 11 in September 2024, and its assets were sold, partly to Akamai. B2B infrastructure with little consumer awareness.

Metagenomi is a California biotechnology company, based in Emeryville, developing gene editing therapies using novel CRISPR systems discovered from metagenomic sequencing and machine learning. Its pipeline targets genetic diseases such as haemophilia A and hereditary angioedema, with collaborations with Moderna, Ionis and others. Founded in 2018 and listed on Nasdaq in 2024 (MGX). Pre-revenue biotech with funding of roughly 467 million dollars. No consumer visibility.

NEAR is a blockchain protocol and platform developed by the NEAR Foundation and Near Inc., designed for scalable decentralised applications and AI agents, with a sharded proof-of-stake network and the NEAR token. It was founded in 2018 by Illia Polosukhin and Alexander Skidanov, who had worked in machine learning, and is based in San Francisco, with backers including a16z, Pantera and Tiger Global. Funding of about 534 million dollars. Known in the crypto community; consumer awareness is limited.

about: o9 Solutions is a Dallas-based provider of cloud planning software, the o9 Digital Brain platform, for demand planning, supply chain, revenue management and integrated business planning, used by large consumer goods, retail and industrial companies. Founded in 2009 by Sanjiv Sidhu, it was valued at about 3.7 billion dollars in 2021, backed by KKR, Generation Investment Management and others. B2B enterprise software, known in supply chain circles, with no consumer visibility.

PagerDuty is a San Francisco-based digital operations management platform that alerts engineering teams about incidents, coordinates response and automates workflows, with AI features, used by thousands of companies including large enterprises. Founded in 2009, it listed on the NYSE in 2019 (PD), with revenue near 450 million dollars. Customers pay subscriptions. B2B developer tool brand with strong recognition among software and IT operations teams, none among general consumers.

Builder.ai was a London-based no-code, AI-assisted software development company, founded in 2016 as Engineer.ai, which promised to assemble custom apps from reusable templates using an AI assistant called Natasha. Backed by Microsoft, the Qatar Investment Authority and SoftBank-linked funds, it raised about 445 million dollars and was valued above 1 billion dollars. In 2025 it entered insolvency after lenders seized cash and questions arose about its reported revenue. No longer operating; it was known mainly in tech media.

about: Dragos is an industrial cybersecurity company that protects operational technology (OT) networks in power plants, utilities, manufacturing and oil and gas through its Dragos Platform, threat intelligence and incident response services. Founded in 2016 by Robert M. Lee and based in Hanover, Maryland, it is backed by Koch Disruptive Technologies, BlackRock and Energy Impact Partners, with funding of about 440 million dollars. B2B security brand with strong standing among industrial operators.

IronNet Cybersecurity was a Vienna, Virginia network detection and response company founded in 2014 by General Keith Alexander, former NSA director, offering collective defence with behaviour analytics for companies and governments. It listed on the NYSE through a SPAC in 2021 (IRNT), but sales slowed and it filed for Chapter 11 in October 2023, with assets sold. Funding around 428 million dollars. B2B and government security brand; no longer operating independently.

Polygon is a blockchain network and ecosystem for scaling Ethereum, launched in 2017 as Matic Network by founders in India and used by apps such as Aave and Uniswap and by brand projects from companies such as Starbucks, Nike and Reddit. Its POL token supports Polygon PoS, zkEVM and the AggLayer. The company has been backed by Sequoia India and Tiger Global, among others. Known in crypto circles, where it has done sports partnerships.

about: SellersFi is a New York-based fintech that provides financing to e-commerce sellers, using AI-driven credit scoring and integration with marketplaces such as Amazon to offer working capital, inventory financing and flexible repayment. Founded in 2020, it raised debt and equity funding worth about 410 million dollars including credit facilities. Customers are online merchants. B2B fintech brand known among marketplace sellers, with no consumer visibility.

about: SoundHound AI is a Santa Clara, California voice artificial intelligence company, founded in 2005 as a music recognition app, now selling voice assistants and conversational AI to automakers (Hyundai, Kia, Stellantis), restaurants (via the Amelia/SoundHound Chat AI and ordering services), and customer service teams. It listed on Nasdaq in 2022 through a SPAC (SOUN) and acquired Amelia in 2024. Revenue is around 100 million dollars. Consumer app SoundHound is known, but business model is B2B.

YouGov is a British market research and data analytics company, founded in 2000 by Stephan Shakespeare and Nadhim Zahawi and headquartered in London. It runs online panels of millions of people to produce polls, brand tracking, and consumer data through products like YouGov Profiles and BrandIndex. Customers are brands, media, agencies and governments. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (YOU), with revenue over 400 million pounds. Public-facing political polls give it high awareness among media audiences.

AEye is a Pleasanton, California lidar company that develops adaptive, high-performance lidar systems for automotive, trucking and industrial applications, for example the Apollo and 4Sight products, using software-defined scanning. It listed on Nasdaq through a SPAC with CF Finance Acquisition Corp. III in 2021 (LIDR), and shifted to licensing and an industrial focus in later years. Funding of around 364 million dollars. B2B sensor supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

Chronosphere is a cloud-native observability platform headquartered in New York that helps engineering teams monitor and control metrics, traces and logs and cost of data. Founded in 2019 by former Uber engineers Martin Mao and Rob Skillington, it serves large companies such as DoorDash, Snap and Robinhood, and was valued at about 1.6 billion dollars in 2022. In late 2025, Palo Alto Networks agreed to acquire it for about 3.35 billion dollars. B2B software with no consumer visibility.

Cloud.ru is a Moscow-based Russian cloud services and AI provider, formerly the Cloud Solutions arm of Sberbank, offering cloud infrastructure, platform and artificial intelligence services (Evolution) to Russian enterprises and government. It was set up as a Sber subsidiary after Sber's reorganisation. Funding is shown in roubles (30 billion). Subject to Western sanctions pressures on Russian tech. B2B IT brand with no consumer awareness.

about: CloudPay is a London-based global payroll services and software provider, managing payroll for multinational companies across around 130 countries via its unified platform and local partners. Founded in 2008, it is owned by private equity firms including Searchlight Capital and Summit Partners, with funding of about 375 million dollars. Customers are multinational HR and finance teams. B2B brand known in the payroll industry, with no consumer visibility.

CoachHub is a Berlin-based digital coaching platform founded in 2018 by Matti Niebelschuetz and Yannis Niebelschuetz, offering corporate employees access to certified coaches by video and an AI coaching assistant, AIMY. It serves large enterprises across more than 70 countries and over 3,500 coaches, and was valued at about 1 billion dollars after Series C in 2022 backed by Highland Europe and Partech. B2B HR tech brand.
